For your PROJECT, the real challenge is tokens, rate limits and retries. A common issue: only testing the happy path, so the first expired token or timeout breaks the sync silently.

My plan: first, review the API docs, limits and auth flow of the other system. Then, build the integration with retries, logging and duplicate checks. Finally, test failures, timeouts and expired tokens before switching it on.

I've done integration work before, and the first thing I check on a project like yours is expiring tokens and rate limits.

A few questions to better understand the scope:
1. Does your plan on each service include API access? Some plans lock the API, better to know before building.
2. Sync one way first, two-way later? I'd recommend one way first, two-way sync needs conflict rules.
3. Is there a busy hour when most records come in? I size batching and rate limits around that peak, not the average.

Ankit

source.description:
I need a reliable Python-based bot whose single purpose is to integrate several external APIs and keep the data flowing between them without manual intervention. The core of the job is to build clean, well-structured code that can:

• Authenticate against each service (OAuth2, token, or key as required)  
• Schedule and trigger calls at configurable intervals  
• Parse and combine the responses into a single, usable JSON payload  
• Log every request/response and gracefully handle time-outs, rate limits, and other common errors

If asynchronous techniques (aiohttp, asyncio) or task queues (Celery, RQ) would improve performance, feel free to include them. Well-written docstrings, a short README, and concise setup instructions are part of the final hand-off so I can extend the bot internally later.

I’m open on exact tooling, as long as the end result is a self-contained script or small package I can drop onto a Linux server and run with a single command. Please include a brief outline of your proposed approach and any past projects where you wired multiple APIs together successfully.
